column1: # The queries the site's search must answer, and the page that owns each.
# scripts/check_search.sh runs every line against the index the site actually
# publishes and fails when the expected page is not in the first few results.
# The file exists because search quality is the one part of the site nothing
# else checks: mkdocs --strict proves every link resolves and says nothing
# about whether a reader can find the page at all, and a search that quietly
# stops answering a query is invisible until somebody gives up looking.
# Format: query <TAB> expected location prefix, and optionally <TAB> n to
# widen the default tolerance of three. Blank lines and # are skipped. The
# prefix may name a page (`29-concurrency/`) or one section of one
# (`F-rosetta-cookbook/#recipe-40`). Add a line whenever a page is added or a
# topic moves; a query here is a promise the site keeps, and a widened
# tolerance is a limit recorded rather than hidden.
# Three kinds of query, because readers arrive three ways (book/README.md):
# by the C# API already in their head, by the C++ spelling, and by what is
# `Task.Run` is two of the commonest words in a book of exercises: `task*`
# matches every "The task" heading and `run*` most instructions, and no tag
# can lift the recipe without hijacking both words for the whole site. The
# wider tolerance is the honest record of that - the recipe is findable, just
# not first, and Appendix F's own index table is the route that works.
# --- Reaching from what is on the screen -------------------------------
